data.title: Disney creates chief technology officer role
data.description:
Disney (DIS) has tapped the former CEO of Character.AI Karandeep Anand as chief technology officer, a newly-created role to advance Disney’s efforts to modernize its technology and assist CEO Josh D’Amaro in his efforts to increase Disney’s digital content.

 Anand will begin his new position October 2, reporting directly to D’Amaro. 

As chief technology officer, Anand will oversee enterprise technology, infrastructure, data and AI platforms, product, and engineering, working across the company's segment technology teams to further modernize how Disney builds and delivers technology company-wide

“Karandeep brings a rare mix of experience across infrastructure, consumer technology, and AI, and will be a vital addition to Disney’s senior leadership team as we further our three priorities: great storytelling as our North Star, technology in service of creativity, and operating as One Disney," said D'Amaro in a press release announcing Anand's appointment.. 

  Anand will bring with him a number of Character.AI’s technical team.

data.title: Xenon downgraded at Deutsche Bank after pause in depression trials
data.description:
Xenon Pharmaceuticals (XENE) fell 30% to reach its lowest level since November after the company paused enrollment in Phase 3 depression trials for its lead asset, azetukalner, following safety concerns, leading to a downgrade at Deutsche Bank.

Analyst David Hoang downgraded the Canadian biotech to Hold from Buy after the company paused enrollments in multiple late-stage trials for azetukalner in major depressive disorder and bipolar depression in reaction to several neuropsychiatric adverse events, including psychosis. 

However, Xenon (XENE) management argued that the decision was a temporary measure taken as a precaution and there won’t be an impact on ongoing epilepsy studies.The nature of the events, as well as their severity and frequency, were in line with the known safety and tolerability profile of the drug, the company added.

Despite those remarks, Hoang said, “We disagree and believe this impairs the molecule’s overall profile as a potential best-in-class drug that would become the go-to, branded antiseizure medication of choice in focal epilepsy.” The analyst slashed his price target on XENE to $46 from $90 per share.

However, Stifel, Baird, and RBC Capital Markets were among the firms to reaffirm their bullish ratings on the stock.  While the surprising decision leads to uncertainty, "we're confident there’s minimal readthrough to FOS," Stifel analyst Paul Matteis wrote with a Buy rating, according to Bloomberg.

RBC Capital Markets analyst Brian Abrahams reiterated his Outperform rating yet trimmed his price target to $70 from $81, noting, “We believe the core value remains epilepsy and do not see any major risk to the filing timelines or commercial launch.”

Baird analyst Brian Skorney also sounded cautious, lowering his price target to $90 from $97 despite an outperforming rating. “We still think the MDD study is adequately powered into the 1Q topline, and we see low-rate psychosis as an AE neurologists are equipped to manage,” Skorney added.

data.title: JPMorgan chief Jamie Dimon set to attend Trump's state dinner for China's Xi - report
data.description:
JPMorgan Chase (JPM) Chairman and CEO Jamie Dimon is expected to attend a state dinner President Donald Trump is hosting for Chinese leader Xi Jinping next week, according to a media report on Friday.

The head of the U.S.'s largest bank by assets will join other prominent executives, including Nvidia's Jensen Huang and OpenAI's Sam Altman, at the dinner in Washington on Thursday, Sept. 24, CNBC reported, citing a source familiar with the matter.

The Wall Street bank has been operating in China for over a hundred years. It opened its first branch in China in 1921. In 2020, J.P. Morgan received approval from the China Securities Regulatory Commission to increase its stake in J.P. Morgan Futures Company Limited to 100%. Its J.P. Morgan Securities (China) Company Limited, the company's majority-owned securities company, started operations in March 2020.

data.title: Array Technologies plunges as UBS downgrades, seeing less available cash for M&A
data.description:
Array Technologies (ARRY) sinks 7.2% in Friday's trading as UBS downgraded the solar tracking manufacturer to Neutral from Buy with a $5 price target, slashed from $10, as the bank expects the use of preferred dividend payments through 2030 to reduce available cash for completing acquisitions.

"The transition of preferred dividends from payment-in-kind to cash-pay changes the outlook for FCF deployment" by reducing "cash available for deleveraging and growth investment, particularly opportunistic M&A, while competitors broaden their platforms through consolidation," UBS analyst Jon Windham said in a note.

The analyst said he expects Array (ARRY) will generate sufficient free cash flow to service the preferred dividends and estimates $162M of cumulative cash payments through 2030, but the company may have less flexibility to expand its product offering and defend its competitive position, increasing the company's reliance on organic growth and execution to deliver upside.

Windham said he remains positive on the direction of the U.S. solar industry, particularly for companies with domestic manufacturing footprints such as Array (ARRY), but he views the stock as fairly valued at ~5x estimated FY 2027 EV/EBITDA.
